conviction_note: The in-window print is the FY2026 Annual Report, which carries no new operating information: every FY26 number is already out through four Appendix 5B quarterlies, the 9 Jul result and the 21 Sep presentation, which quotes the FY26 A$25M tax expense. The only live content is the Annual Mineral Resource & Ore Reserve statement and the initial Mainfield reserve the company says will come 'end of September'. Its ounces probably hold or grow on a higher gold price, but the FY26 underground grade mined (2.67-3.35 g/t) is far below the 5.0 g/t underground reserve grade, and the 5-year plan re-rate was pushed to the December quarter on 21 Sep. So I size a small negative, discounted for the roughly 35% chance the statement lands on 30 Sep, outside the window, and for a stock already +10.8pp ahead of the ASX gold index over 20 days.
bar: The company's own last statement: Ore Reserve 859koz @ 2.1 g/t, underground 360koz @ 5.0 g/t, as at 30 Jun 2025 (Annual MROR 22 Sep 2025, restated in the 30 Jul 2026 quarterly Appendix 2: https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260730/pdf/0726h8dzz80wmp.pdf). The financial bar is the Appendix 5B figures already published. There is no street consensus in the baseline, and no two agreeing estimate sources on reserves, so every size is capped small.
filer_type_check: Baseline says 'results', but Pantoro lodges Appendix 5B quarterlies, which makes it a mining exploration entity. It lodges no 4D or 4E (none in the 2024-2026 archive); it lodges a half-year report about 68-72 days after period end and an Annual Report in late September. So the print is the Annual Report, whose numbers are pre-disclosed, and I hunted the Mineral Resource & Ore Reserve update and any guidance change that could ride with it instead of EPS.
event_check: There is no forward 'results date' notice. Confirmed by pattern and deadline. The 2024 Annual Report was lodged 26/09/2024 16:10 and the 2025 one 25/09/2025 16:16, both after the close. The 2026 one has not been lodged as of 25/09/2026 (the last row is a Norges Bank Form 603 at 08:11), and the Corporations Act deadline for a June-year-end disclosing entity is 30/09/2026. The 21/09/2026 Operations Update says 'Annual Mineral Resource & Ore Reserve statement to be released end of September'. A print on 28, 29 or 30 Sep is near-certain; 28 Sep specifically is vendor-only. Settled on the issuer's own habit: both prior Annual Reports were lodged between 16:10 and 16:20 Sydney, after the 16:00 close (2025 rows at https://www.asx.com.au/asx/v2/statistics/announcements.do?by=asxCode&asxCode=PNR&timeframe=Y&year=2025). The Mineral Resource & Ore Reserve statement has come at 08:29-08:30 (22/09/2025, 26/09/2024). If it comes 28 Sep 08:30 it is before the window; 29 Sep 08:30 is inside it.
positioning_check: ASIC aggregate short is 1.41% as of 2026-09-21, down from 2.12% on 2026-09-14 (-0.71pp). Shorts are covering, and the register is 4 sessions stale. Over the same stretch the stock went from A$2.60 (11 Sep) to A$2.94 while the ASX gold index was flat. It is +6.1% over 5 days against -0.9% for the index, and +2.1% over 20 days against -8.7%, about 10.8pp of excess. 1.4% is not a crowded short, so there is no squeeze fuel. The covering is consistent with the rally that has already happened. A Norges Bank Form 603 at 5.43% on 25 Sep is securities-lending collateral churn (Appendix A is almost all 'Collateral Shares Received/Returned'), not a buyer.

findings.finding: The Ore Reserve statement due 'end of September' has to reconcile a year in which underground ore was mined at 2.67/3.35/2.92/2.94 g/t (FY26 Q1-Q4) against a 5.0 g/t underground reserve grade. The quarterly also reports OK seismicity and 'closing pillar' problems in the final central-access levels. That points to downside in underground reserve grade and ounces, partly offset by open-pit additions at a higher price deck (Gladstone Stage 3 and Daisy South approved, Green Lantern restarted) and an initial Mainfield reserve that management has already framed as 'only a small portion ... accessed for assessment'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Prior Mineral Resource & Ore Reserve days, measured against the ASX gold index (^AXGD) on the baseline's Yahoo tape: 26/09/2024 (statement plus Annual Report the same day) PNR +4.55% vs index +1.52%, excess +3.03; 22/09/2025 PNR +7.53% vs +6.74%, excess +0.79. The day after the 2025 Annual Report (26/09/2025) was excess +4.69, in a gold bull market. So the reserve line has not been sold on the two observed prints. By contrast, every operational or guidance disclosure in 2026 was sold hard: 10/03 -24.6 excess, 09/07 -8.9, 22/01 -5.6, 28/04 -8.5.
findings.why_not_priced: The quarterly grades are public, but nobody publishes a reserve-grade reconciliation for this name. The baseline carries no consensus and the reserve line has twice been bought, which is what a market that is not worried about the underground reserve looks like. If the risk were priced, PNR would not be running 10.8pp ahead of the gold index into the release with shorts covering from 2.12% to 1.41%. The upside half of this finding (price-deck additions) is the more obvious read, which is why the net is small and not large.
findings.independence: The 21/09/2026 presentation (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260921/pdf/0749f6zytkwwch.pdf) is a separate document from the same issuer. It moves the 5-year plan from 'alongside the annual Mineral Resource and Ore Reserve statement' in the Sep quarter (9 Jul release, https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260709/pdf/071k8zzbxhcfk8.pdf) to the December quarter, and it calls Mainfield 'only a small portion ... accessed'. That is expectation management consistent with a statement that will not re-rate the stock by itself. It is the same issuer, so only partly independent.

outside_window.finding: Updated five-year production plan including Racetrack (4.94m @ 349 g/t; 43-hole average 3.58m @ 18.59 g/t), moved from the Sep quarter to the Dec quarter on 21 Sep. This is the real re-rating catalyst in either direction.

September-quarter production: 19,130 oz as of 19 Sep, which extrapolates to about 21-22koz against H1 guidance of 40-45% of 90-105koz (36-47koz), so on track. Reported in the late-October quarterly, which is outside the window.

searched_and_found_nothing: ASX archive 2024-2026 for a trading halt, guidance update, capital raise or Appendix 3B around the print: none since 20/07/2026 (a proposed issue of securities, employee-scale).
Buyback as a support: the 30 Jul quarterly says it was 'temporarily reduced'. There have been no Update-Notification of buy-back rows since 24/06/2026.

Substantial holders: Norges Bank 5.43% (25/09) is lending collateral. Holder changes through Aug-Sep are the usual passive/lending churn, with no director buying or selling since the 18/08 Appendix 3Y (performance-rights vesting context).

Impairment or tax surprise in the Annual Report: FY26 was profitable at A$6,293/oz sold vs AISC A$3,139-4,107, operating cash flow A$272.8m, and the tax expense (A$25M) is already disclosed in the 21 Sep deck.

Press and broker coverage (Proactive, Kalkine, Motley Fool AU, The Bull, Discovery Alert): only restated company releases. The Bull reports a trimmed consensus target of A$5.14 from A$5.82 (https://thebull.com.au/news/pantoro-gold-shares-close-above-a3-for-the-first-time-in-months-is-momentum-shifting/), with no reserve expectation quoted.
S&P DJI Sept 2026 rebalance notice (04/09) and 18/09 volume spike (15.1M): consistent with index-rebalance trading and not a company event.
baseline_tension: The finding leans slightly against the +2.16 priced lean and the +6.1% 5-day run-up, but it is small and two-sided. The relative strength and short covering already bank the good news, which is why the negative is kept small instead of being built into a contrarian call.
